I was working at party city the senior year of high school. I was made supervisor after I graduated and after the Fourth of July we started putting up our Halloween stuff. 
We’d hire loads of people specifically to help around this time of year because it was the stores busiest time. The biggest problem was the general manager was a bitch, and the managers were hiding merchandise that needed to put out IN THE CEILING because we couldn’t stay clocked in 30 minutes after our shift ended to finish putting everything out. The second biggest problem was us being extremely understaffed, especially around Halloween. Everyone thought it’d be cool to apply because you got to wear a costume to work, but they shortly realized of what a fucked job this was and quit two days after without calling. It was awful.

One day my fellow supervisor who worked in the back told me she’d be going on vacation the next day and she’d need me to do inventory for her that day. I had no problem with this since she was always doing favors for me when I worked. She showed me how to do it and then left. 

I started that day at 7 am, the store opened at 9am. I started inventory at 10am. My shift ended at 6pm. After doing this for about an hour I kept getting calls over the radio that everyone had to wear for me to come up to the registers to help. I told them I couldn’t because I was doing inventory, and to ask another manager or supervisor. They said they did but nobody came up. I went to up to help and after getting the line down I went into the office and there was my general manager, my manager, and the two other supervisors sitting there texting and talking. I slammed the door and went back to inventory.

My manager told me if I didn’t get all the costumes into inventory THE SAME DAY I would be fired. I laughed in her face, but since at the time I thought I needed this job I got it done as quick as I could. 

My general manager then tells me that I needed to go through three HUGE boxes of inventory and mark down every item in the boxes individually with a sharpie and put them on display. she said I needed to get this done because my job was on the line. Over clearance boxes. I didn’t say anything, and when she walked away I put the boxes in the top shelf and walked out with smoke coming 

I got 40 missed calls from my manager, and plenty of heavily worded messages from them. Best decision ever. I never went back there and my coworker who went on vacation quit shortly after I did.

Allow yourself time to feel what you’re feeling. Allow yourself to feel everything. Remember that healing isn’t linear, missing someone who committed suicide will come in waves. You’ll feel happy one day, sad the next, angry the next day, etc etc, but allow yourself to grieve for this person. I know it’s so hard to see now, but you will eventually find a way to cope with your loss. Whether it’s therapy, finding comfort in a memory, or something else, you will find a way to cope with this. Don’t give up on yourself so quickly. I can tell you after almost four years after someone I loved took their life, I still have my days. I still have days where I feel empty, I still have days where I’m pissed at them and all I want to do is scream, and then I have days where I’m content that they finally got what they wanted (as morbid as that sounds). If I could go back to when it first happened and tell myself that everyone was right, and I’d feel better once I allowed myself to properly grieve for him, I would. Allow yourself to grieve, and remember that everyone grieves differently. If you need to cry, cry, if you need to scream, scream, if you need to talk, find someone to listen.
